payload: {"schema":1,"version":"0.0.48","date":"2026-10-07","lede":"Render region raytraces only a part of the view; Color correct v3 works like Lightroom\u2019s develop panel; artists can publish their exhibitions from the Exhibitions tab.","highlights":["Render region","Artist pages and exhibitions","More functions for buttons","Fog over the backplate"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.48","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Render region","b":"Render region limits raytracing to a rectangle over the view, and the rest of the view shows the normal viewport. Drag the handle below the rectangle, or its dashed frame, to move it, and drag its corners or edge handles to resize it; Shift keeps its proportions. A bar above the rectangle appears when the pointer is over it and sets the region\u2019s resolution (full, half, quarter or eighth), pauses or resumes it, switches the outside between Unlit, Raster and Dim, and closes the region. A paused region keeps its image and turns grey if the view changes.","w":["Lighting tab \u203a Raytrace \u203a Region render","Add function \u203a Display \u203a Render region"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Artist pages and exhibitions","b":"Artists with a Klay licence open their artist page from the Exhibitions tab and manage it on klaysculpt.com: their profile, an optional year of birth, and their exhibitions. Featured artists are shown in the gallery\u2019s rail, and each exhibition shows its number of visitors.","w":["Welcome screen \u203a Exhibitions \u203a My artist page"],"n":"Licence required"},{"g":"n","t":"More functions for buttons","b":"The function picker offers 29 more functions for the sidebar, the viewport action bar and the radial menus. Display: Faceted shading, Wireframe, Ground grid, Orthographic, Raytracing, Cycle shading mode, Focus mode, X-ray selected and Viewport HUD. Symmetry: X, Y, Z, Radial and Edit symmetry plane. Object and levels: Align, Mirror +X / \u2212X, Flip normals, Group, Ungroup, Unparent, Frame selected, Level up / down, Delete higher levels, Flatten levels and Tessellation. Also Export OBJ (highest level) and Add camera. Toggles light up while they are on.","w":["Add function \u203a Display / Symmetry / Object / Topology / Camera"]},{"g":"n","t":"Fog over the backplate","b":"Composite volumetric renders the scene\u2019s volumetric fog in front of a camera\u2019s backplate image, so the plate sits inside the atmosphere instead of behind a flat layer. The plate\u2019s Depth sets how much fog is in front of it. Applies in Raytrace shading with scene fog enabled.","w":["Camera tab \u203a Image plane \u203a Composite volumetric"]},{"g":"i","t":"Color correct v3","b":"Color correct now works much like Lightroom\u2019s develop panel. Sections follow Lightroom\u2019s order: Light, Curve, Color, Grading, Effects, Detail and Grain. Clarity, Structure and Dehaze now take the whole image into account, so local contrast stays free of halos around large forms and Dehaze adapts to the haze in the frame. Clarity and Structure also accept negative values, which soften the image. Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Temp, Vibrance and Saturation use Lightroom-style responses, and readouts show signed values from \u2212100 to +100. Shift-drag a slider for fine adjustment; after clicking a slider, the Up and Down arrow keys nudge it while the pointer stays over it. The Shadows, Midtones and Highlights wheels are unchanged.","w":["Post tab \u203a Color correct","Camera tool \u203a Grade"],"n":"Clarity, Structure and sharpening are desktop only"},{"g":"i","t":"Shortcuts: swap Ctrl and Alt, mouse buttons","b":"Swap Ctrl and Alt exchanges the two keys everywhere: every Ctrl shortcut becomes Alt and every Alt shortcut becomes Ctrl, including Ctrl-click to invert a brush and Alt + drag to navigate. Any shortcut can also be set to the middle mouse button or the side buttons (Mouse 4 and 5), for example to open the radial hub with the middle button. A mouse button already used by a navigation chord is refused.","w":["Settings \u203a Navigation \u203a Global navigation","Shortcuts tab \u203a any shortcut"]},{"g":"i","t":"Curve tool: end tapers, profile grid","b":"Taper start and Taper end now narrow each end of a curve separately, each with its own length. The profile editor has an adjustable grid that points can snap to; hold Shift while dragging to place a point freely. The shortcut that removes a point can be changed in the Shortcuts tab.","w":["Curve tool \u203a Along the curve","Curve tool \u203a Profile","Shortcuts tab \u203a Tools"]},{"g":"i","t":"Stamp & Falloff: shape, then spacing","b":"The Stroke section is now part of Stamp & Falloff, ordered by the choices you make. Shape is Procedural (Circular, Box or Crease, each with its own settings below it) or Alpha. A single Spacing slider replaces the Polywire switch, Spaced stamps and Bead spacing: its far-left zone is Polywire, the smooth swept line, with its settings shown below it; the next zone is Continuous, a line of overlapping dabs; further right the shape is printed that far apart, in percent of the brush size, for every shape, up to ten times the brush size. Imprint, Direction and Dynamics follow, and the other technical stroke settings are grouped in Advanced stroke. Dynamics now has Taper start next to Taper end; Taper end works on polygon meshes: the stroke trails the cursor by the taper length and finishes it to a point after you release, and the Spacing preview shows the loaded alpha and every Dynamics setting. Each setting has an information button that explains it. Existing brushes keep their previous behaviour.","w":["Brush tab \u203a Stamp & Falloff"]},{"g":"i","t":"Pen pressure","b":"Poly brushes have a Pen pressure section. Size, Strength, Hardness, Smooth and Elastique each have a switch, a range from a light touch to a full press, and their own response curve. Settings \u203a Tablet adds an app-wide pressure curve, a threshold below which nothing is drawn, a full-at point and pressure smoothing. Existing brushes keep their previous response.","w":["Brush tab \u203a Pen pressure","Settings \u203a Tablet \u203a Pressure feel"]},{"g":"i","t":"Brush cursor settings","b":"A Brush cursor section sets the ring colours, the fade while stroking, the centre dot size and the system pointer. For brushes whose size follows pressure, the ring shows the light-touch size and a dotted ring the full-press size; a few dots keep the full-press size visible during a stroke.","w":["Settings \u203a Brush cursor"]},{"g":"i","t":"Orbit around mouse point","b":"A new navigation option orbits around the surface under the mouse when the orbit starts. Over empty space, the previous point is kept. It replaces Orbit around stroke point when turned on; F returns to the usual centre.","w":["Settings \u203a Navigation \u203a Behaviour"]},{"g":"i","t":"More than 8 lights","b":"A scene is no longer limited to 8 lights. Raytrace lights the scene with every light; the viewport shades the first 8. Lights beyond the eighth do not use a projector Source, an IES profile or Raytrace caustics. The Lantern light list now shows every light without scrolling.","w":["Lantern tool \u203a Lights","Lighting tab \u203a Lights"]},{"g":"i","t":"Lighting presets grow as you fill them","b":"Presets and Scene presets always show complete rows, and a new row of empty slots appears as soon as one in the last row is used. A scene is no longer limited to 12 Scene presets.","w":["Lighting tab \u203a Presets","Lighting tab \u203a Scene presets"]},{"g":"f","t":"After a Laser cut with Fill, the cap is now welded to the mesh, so smoothing across the cut no longer splits it open."},{"g":"f","t":"When an update is available, its Download & install button now always stays visible at the bottom of the welcome screen, and long release notes scroll above it."},{"g":"f","t":"With Raytrace on, changing the Room disk or a backdrop's parameters no longer makes the other objects disappear from the view."},{"g":"f","t":"Enabling Coat, Emission, or Subsurface on a material in the Raytrace view no longer produces a brief bright flash before the image settles."},{"g":"f","t":"Switching from Unlit back to Raytrace no longer occasionally drops instanced objects from the view."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, Gizmo \u203a Consider masking now poses each mirrored copy of the unmasked area about its own mirrored pivot, and a scale bead now scales along its own axis only."},{"g":"f","t":"On a polygon mesh with symmetry on, including topology symmetry, Ctrl+left-drag rotation and Ctrl+right-drag scaling with a Grab brush now apply to the mirrored side as well."},{"g":"f","t":"Holding X for a momentary Mask brush now switches instantly."},{"g":"f","t":"On polygon meshes, alpha brushes with Imprint or Spaced stamps keep the full detail of the alpha and use the same strength scale as a stroke; non-square alphas keep their proportions, and stamps along a stroke no longer smear."},{"g":"f","t":"With Orbit set to a mouse button without a modifier (for example the right button), pressing Shift during the orbit now snaps to the axis views."},{"g":"f","t":"Exhibitions now show only the mouse pointer, even when a clay stamp was selected before entering, and open with the artist\u2019s Smooth or Faceted normals setting instead of the visitor\u2019s."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Camera tool, the Converging notice shown while a capture waits for the Raytrace image now appears in the same place as the saved-capture notice, fully on screen."}],"windows":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.48/Klay_Setup_0.0.48.exe","size":413843213,"sha512":"da0fbf936fff84942d211920e6bd709614079f72d4362e554f9d589bb0f01b63a3ba65d192cbea0e7a35b46068a722716774abbb59ff13b8dc736fe07034492c"},"history":[{"version":"0.0.47","date":"2026-10-06","lede":"A Camera tool, a new Curve tool, Exhibitions and locked scenes, camera tracks, and sequence renders and movies.","highlights":["Camera tool","Curve tool","Exhibitions and locked scenes","Speakers","Brush mixer and Global brush settings","Camera tracks","Cameras in the viewport","Camera monitor","Sequence render and movies","Camera aspect ratio","Video on the Canvas","Extrude mask","Posing with the gizmo","Compare","Material bindings","Per-object display","Transform menu","Rotator","Update review","Viewport action bar","Rain water effects"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.47","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Camera tool","b":"The Camera tool turns the view into a camera viewfinder, with shutter, aperture, ISO, focal length and focus in a bar along the bottom. Clicking in the view sets the focus point, which stays sharp as you orbit, and the capture button saves the framed view and adds it to the Canvas. The Look button opens collapsible sections for the frame format, view transform, colour grade, raytracing samples, secondary bounces and sharpening, the denoiser (GPU or CPU, with its strength) and the overlays (rule of thirds, safe frame, level, histogram); Linear and AgX Punchy are new view transforms. The Auto button sets auto exposure, its metering, compensation and adaptation. Both are also available in an exhibition\u2019s Camera mode.","w":["Tools \u203a Camera"],"n":"Esc or Tab returns to sculpting; desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Curve tool","b":"The Curve tool draws a stroke and sweeps a profile along it as an editable mesh. Profiles are preset shapes or custom outlines with sharp, filleted or chamfered corners, and the card sets taper, twist, caps and a hollow wall. Physics lets dragged points swing or stretch the curve, Brushing reshapes many curves at once, and Bake turns a curve into a sculpt layer. Thickness changes along the curve blend smoothly into each other. The Smooth section relaxes the whole tube while keeping its volume, from a light touch to a very strong smoothing. Holding Ctrl turns the curve under the cursor red; a click deletes it, and dragging deletes every curve the cursor crosses.","w":["Tools \u203a Curve"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Exhibitions and locked scenes","b":"File \u203a Save as Exhibition saves a .klaylock: an encrypted, view-only copy of the scene with its textures, HDRI, backplates and sounds packed inside. It opens with only Orbit, Walk and Camera, where Camera mode uses the Camera tool\u2019s strip and shutter, and cannot be edited or exported. When the artist allows it, the bottom bar also offers a view menu (Unlit, PBR, PBR full, Raytrace) and a Scene button that switches between the scene\u2019s lighting presets and material bindings. Scene presets can be renamed in the Lighting tab with a right-click or a double-click. The artist\u2019s cameras are not shown. The home screen\u2019s new Exhibitions tab lists curated locked scenes. Each work carries a piece number, such as KL.2026.001, and each artist has a profile page with a header image, portrait and biography. Open in browser, at the foot of the gallery\u2019s list, opens the exhibitions on klaysculpt.com, where each work offers Open in Klay and Download. The sun and moon button at the top of the gallery switches it between light and dark. Settings \u203a Exhibition \u203a Culture is not my friend removes the Exhibitions tab from the home screen; it is off by default.","w":["File \u203a Save as Exhibition","Home screen \u203a Exhibitions"],"n":"Videos are not packed; desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Speakers","b":"A speaker plays an MP3 or WAV file inside a sphere in the scene, heard from its position as you orbit, walk or look around in VR. Each speaker sets its radius, volume, soft edge, looping, and what happens when you enter or leave it. A button mutes every speaker while you work.","w":["Room tab \u203a Add \u203a Speaker"]},{"g":"n","t":"Brush mixer and Global brush settings","b":"The Mixer card blends three brushes of the same family on a triangle: drag the point toward a corner to give that brush more weight, and every setting of the three is blended into the brush in use. The card\u2019s switch turns the mix on or off, and Save as brush keeps the result as a new preset. The Global card scales one operator, such as Smooth, across every Clay or Poly brush, from muted to double, with a single pressure response and Reset all.","w":["Brush tab \u203a Mixer / Global"],"n":"Clay and Poly brushes"},{"g":"n","t":"Camera tracks","b":"A camera can follow a track over a block of frames on the timeline. Tracks are drawn point by point or recorded by moving the view, then smoothed, resampled or edited with the gizmo. Each camera adds handheld drift, shake, lag and focus breathing, and keys for focal length, exposure, aperture and a focus point.","w":["Camera tab \u203a Track"],"n":"Recording is desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Cameras in the viewport","b":"Other cameras are drawn in the viewport with their field of view and an optional name. With the Select, Move or Gizmo tool, clicking a camera selects it and the gizmo moves it; dropping it near a track places it on that track.","w":["Camera tab \u203a Camera card header"]},{"g":"n","t":"Camera monitor","b":"A small monitor in a corner of the viewport shows the view through the active camera, in Unlit, PBR Fast or Raytrace shading. It can follow the timeline, the selected camera or a pinned one, and can be moved, resized or collapsed.","w":["Camera tab \u203a Monitor"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Sequence render and movies","b":"A render job can be a Still or a Sequence. A sequence renders one camera\u2019s block, or the whole timeline through the camera cuts, with In and Out handles to trim it. Output is MP4 (H.264 or H.265), ProRes 422 HQ or 4444, or an image sequence.","w":["Render tab \u203a Job card"],"n":"MP4 uses the graphics card\u2019s video encoder; ProRes works on every machine"},{"g":"n","t":"Camera aspect ratio","b":"Each camera has an aspect ratio, from 2.39:1 to the portrait 9:16. The Camera tool shows it as the frame, and renders that follow the camera use it. In the Render tab, a job\u2019s Format lists the same ratios beside Camera, and Size sets the long edge; Custom starts from the current size.","w":["Camera tab \u203a Format \u203a Aspect"]},{"g":"n","t":"Video on the Canvas","b":"Movies sent from the Render tab, and MP4 or MOV files dropped on the Canvas, play as video cards with a player bar, frame steps, speed and loop. Save frame places the current frame on the board as a PNG.","w":["Render tab \u203a Output \u203a Send to canvas"]},{"g":"n","t":"Extrude mask","b":"The masked area of a polygon mesh can be extruded into a separate shell, with thickness, direction, smoothing and a rim shape, previewed live on the model. The result is a new layer, or is merged into or cut into the source mesh.","w":["Outliner \u203a Right-click a mesh \u203a Extrude mask"],"n":"Needs a painted mask; desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Posing with the gizmo","b":"With Consider masking on, the Gizmo tool moves, rotates or scales only the unmasked part of a polygon mesh about the pivot, so a limb can be posed from its joint. A padlock beside the gizmo unlocks the pivot: the gizmo then moves and turns only itself, and the pivot\u2019s position and orientation are saved with the object.","w":["Tools \u203a Gizmo \u203a Consider masking"],"n":"Masking applies to polygon meshes; Clay layers move as a whole"},{"g":"n","t":"Compare","b":"Selected objects and groups go into a list and are shown one at a time with a slider or Prev and Next. Layout places them side by side in a row, grid or column, and Bake positions keeps the arrangement.","w":["Outliner \u203a Right-click an object or group \u203a Compare"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Material bindings","b":"A scene can keep several sets of material assignments and switch between them with one click. The materials are shared by all sets; each set records which material each object wears. The plus button adds a copy of the current set, the name under the buttons can be edited, and right-clicking a number duplicates, moves or deletes that set. Sets are saved with the scene.","w":["Material tab \u203a Bindings"]},{"g":"n","t":"Per-object display","b":"Clicking an object\u2019s icon in the outliner sets its colour and how it draws: Shaded, Dither, X-ray, Fill, Wire or Bounds. The same menu sets faceted normals, backfaces, shadows, render visibility and whether it can be selected.","w":["Outliner \u203a Click an object\u2019s icon"]},{"g":"n","t":"Transform menu","b":"A button on each outliner row opens its position, pivot, rotation and scale for typing, in the scene unit. Each channel can be reset or locked, and six slots store transforms; for a group, a slot stores the whole arrangement.","w":["Outliner \u203a Transform button on a row"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Rotator","b":"A rotator turns all objects, or one outliner group, around a vertical axis over a block of frames on the timeline. It is moved with the gizmo, and R returns it to the centre of the scene.","w":["Room tab \u203a Add \u203a Rotator"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Update review","b":"After an update, a review lists what changed in your preferences, settings, brushes and presets before the home screen opens. Your preferences and shortcuts are kept, factory brushes and presets take the new version, and each item can be switched to Keep mine, Take new or Keep both. Brush size, strength and hardness always stay yours, and replaced files are kept in a backup folder.","w":["Settings \u203a Preferences \u203a Updates"],"n":"Shown only when updating an existing installation"},{"g":"n","t":"Viewport action bar","b":"A row of buttons in the lower-right corner of the viewport runs functions in one click; + adds one, right-click replaces or removes it, and press-and-hold reorders. Holding Space shows the bar alone, and releasing Space over a button runs it.","w":["Viewport \u203a Lower-right corner"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"n","t":"Rain water effects","b":"The Rain card now shows only density, speed, wetness, tint and sound, with the rest under Water effects and Advanced. Rain has new water effects, each with its own switch: surfaces under a roof or overhang stay dry, walls facing the rain get wet, water runs down slopes and walls, droplets cling to slopes and slide, drops hang under overhangs, and puddles form on flat ground, filling hollows first. Raindrops can burst into small splashes where they land, and water drips from edges and corners onto the surface below.","w":["Lighting tab \u203a Weather \u203a Rain \u203a Water effects"],"n":"Also rendered in the raytraced view"},{"g":"i","t":"Undo history scrub","b":"Pressing Ctrl+Z twice in quick succession shows a history strip above the toolbar. Drag along it or use the mouse wheel to move through undo and redo steps. A single Ctrl+Z works as before. The strip closes after a few seconds without input, on Esc, or when you make a new edit. Settings > Undo turns it off or changes how many presses open it, and sets how much memory the undo history may use (1 GB by default, up to 16 GB), an optional step limit, and Clear history.","w":["Ctrl+Z \u203a twice quickly"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"i","t":"Typed slider values","b":"Every slider value can now be typed. The number highlights under the pointer; click it, enter a value and press Enter or click elsewhere to apply it, or press Esc to cancel. The value is kept within the slider\u2019s range.","w":["Sidebar, tool cards and tool dialogs"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"i","t":"Gizmo tool card","b":"A Transform section on the Gizmo tool card shows the selection\u2019s position, pivot, rotation, scale and size for typing, with the same locks and actions as the outliner Transform menu. The values update when a drag ends.","w":["Tools \u203a Gizmo \u203a Transform"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"i","t":"Film grain","b":"Film grain is now built from simulated film crystals, with presets for common film stocks, 16 mm, Super 8 and a digital sensor. It can be fixed or animated, and Follow camera ISO sets its strength from the camera\u2019s ISO. In the raytraced view the grain is developed into the image itself.","w":["Post \u203a Film grain"]},{"g":"i","t":"Color correct","b":"The section is reorganised in photo-editor order: White balance, Tone, Curve, Colour, Grading, Detail and Grain. A histogram sits at the top, Before shows the uncorrected image while held, and each section has its own Reset.","w":["Post \u203a Color correct"],"n":"The histogram needs the linear HDR pipeline"},{"g":"i","t":"Brush icon colours","b":"The Pick icon window has a Colour row with the same palette as Canvas groups, plus a custom colour. The icon and its name take the chosen colour on the toolbar, in the slot switcher, in the Vault and on the Brush panel; Default keeps the usual look.","w":["Toolbar \u203a right-click \u203a Pick Icon\u2026"],"n":"Also from the Brush panel icon"},{"g":"i","t":"Settings: Navigation","b":"Orbit, pan and zoom are now set in Settings, each with its own combination of keys and a mouse button; the same controls are on the mouse panel of the keyboard map. A combination can use any key, such as C with the left button, or the middle or right button on its own. The Navigation key can also be any key, such as P: holding it navigates as Alt does. A key used this way is removed from any other shortcut, and the dialog names it before you apply. A new option, Orbit around stroke point, orbits around where the last stroke started; F returns to the usual centre. Void, as in ZBrush, lets a drag on empty space orbit, pan and zoom without holding a key; it turns off Allow outside stroke.","w":["Settings \u203a Navigation"]},{"g":"i","t":"Settings: Interface colors","b":"The Theme card has Panel and Text colors and a Contrast slider. Every surface, border and secondary label follows them, and Text on Auto turns dark on a light panel. Each color, including the accent, can be returned to its default.","w":["Settings \u203a Theme \u203a Interface colors"]},{"g":"i","t":"Settings: Tablet and Scrolling","b":"Tablet chooses how the pen is read: Automatic, Wintab compat or Windows Ink. Scrolling sets one mouse-wheel speed for the whole sidebar, which now scrolls smoothly.","w":["Settings \u203a Tablet","Settings \u203a Scrolling"]},{"g":"i","t":"Live instances of Clay layers","b":"Clay layers now have Instance (live) and Instance X (live): a copy that follows every edit of the original, the second mirrored across X. A live copy adds almost no memory, and Make independent turns it into its own layer.","w":["Outliner \u203a Clay layer menu"]},{"g":"i","t":"Camera card: Format and Exposure","b":"The camera card has a Format sub-card for aspect ratio, bars and guides, and an Exposure sub-card for shutter, ISO, auto exposure and the view transform. Turning on depth of field now also turns on autofocus.","w":["Camera tab \u203a Camera card"]},{"g":"i","t":"Render engines: Raytrace, PBR, Unlit","b":"A render job uses Raytrace, PBR or Unlit. PBR renders now include ambient occlusion, fog, depth of field, bloom and the colour grade, as in the viewport.","w":["Render tab \u203a Job card"]},{"g":"i","t":"Knife: bend the held line","b":"A Knife line held with Shift has a handle at each end that bends it into a curve or a rounded corner, with optional angle snap. Clicking the centre dot cuts, and Latch hold keeps the line up without Shift.","w":["Tools \u203a Laser \u203a Knife"],"n":"Polygon meshes; desktop only"},{"g":"i","t":"Decimation","b":"The Decimation dialog shows progress, and Cancel leaves the mesh unchanged. A GPU mode runs it on the graphics card, and LOD chain builds two to eight lighter copies in one press.","w":["Outliner \u203a Right-click a mesh \u203a Decimation"]},{"g":"i","t":"Emission: temperature and coat","b":"Emission can be set by temperature in kelvin instead of a colour. Under coat places the glow beneath the clear coat, and Light the fog (RT) lets glowing objects light the fog.","w":["Material tab \u203a Emission"]},{"g":"i","t":"Brush size and tessellation sharing","b":"Share size across brushes keeps one size when switching brush, and Share values does the same for tessellation. The Shift brush has a Use primary brush size toggle.","w":["Brush tab"],"n":"Clay and polygon brushes; tessellation is polygon only"},{"g":"i","t":"Stamp depth graph and Dynamic masking","b":"The Stamp brush\u2019s Depth section shows the stamp\u2019s outline at a light and a hard pen press. Dynamic masking generators have a Preview toggle and a Pressure sub-card.","w":["Brush tab"]},{"g":"i","t":"Alpha brush detail","b":"On polygon meshes, an alpha brush now lays the full image as separate stamps along the stroke, at the brush\u2019s Spacing, instead of stretching the centre of the image along the stroke. Overlapping stamps keep their detail, rotation jitter turns each stamp individually, and 16-bit alphas keep their full depth.","w":["Brush tab \u203a Alpha"],"n":"Polygon brushes"},{"g":"i","t":"Photoshop alphas","b":"Brush alphas can be imported from Photoshop files (.psd and .psb, Grayscale or RGB, 8, 16 or 32-bit) and appear in the alpha library with a thumbnail. Klay reads the flattened image, so the file must be saved with Maximize Compatibility on.","w":["Brush tab \u203a Alpha \u203a Import"],"n":"Clay and polygon brushes"},{"g":"i","t":"Faster tabs and raytracing","b":"The Material and Lighting tabs no longer pause on first open, and their thumbnails are kept between sessions. While a slider or light is dragged, the raytracer renders fewer frames so the interface stays responsive. Fog and light beams in the raytraced view clear up faster, with the same final image.","w":["Lighting tab \u203a Raytrace \u203a Responsiveness \u203a Yield to UI"]},{"g":"i","t":"Raytrace settings in groups","b":"The Raytrace settings are grouped into six cards: Quality, Light & image, Material offsets, Effects, Responsiveness and Advanced. A closed card shows a summary of its settings, and options that depend on a switch appear under it only while it is on. Every slider has a reset button.","w":["Lighting tab \u203a Raytrace"]},{"g":"i","t":"Right-click menu: Create","b":"Right-clicking an object opens a Create submenu with Light, Camera and New material. Light adds a Point, Sun, Spot, Area or Camera light placed from the current view, as the Lighting tab\u2019s add button does; Camera adds a camera at the current view, as the Camera tab\u2019s Camera button does; New material creates a material and assigns it to the selected object. Right-clicking an empty scene lists Light and Camera directly in its Create section. The + button in the Scene outliner header opens the same Create entries; Primitive has been removed from it.","w":["Viewport \u203a right-click \u203a Create"],"n":"Desktop only"},{"g":"i","t":"Outliner and File menu","b":"Saved scenes keep which outliner folders are open, and F over the outliner reveals the selection. The File menu now shows keyboard shortcuts.","w":["Scene outliner"]},{"g":"f","t":"Huion and other non-Wacom pen tablets now respond."},{"g":"f","t":"Brush Dynamics on polygon meshes: Scatter places each stamp on the surface without tearing the stroke and now works on every stroke type, each stroke gets its own jitter pattern, pen pressure no longer changes the jitter, and speed settings behave the same at any frame rate."},{"g":"f","t":"A poly brush stroke that starts off the model now begins as soon as the pointer reaches the surface. Brush panel > Stroke > Allow outside stroke, on by default."},{"g":"f","t":"A UI scale below 100% no longer pushes the toolbar and sidebar off the screen. The scale is remembered per screen."},{"g":"f","t":"Pressing Apply in the keyboard map no longer closes Klay."},{"g":"f","t":"Exporting a group writes every object inside it, with each object kept separate in FBX, Alembic and glTF.
